assets.name: Warrior King
assets.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: fresh V2 full-body hero illustration candidate for a fair before/after comparison in the game Arenic. Use the supplied existing portrait as a CHARACTER IDENTITY AND ART-STYLE REFERENCE. Make a genuinely fresh rendering with refined pose, anatomical clarity and expressive detail; do not merely replace its background or return a near-pixel-identical copy. Preserve species, recognisable face, signature costume, gear and established colors. Style: hand-inked medieval fantasy etched woodcut/comic art, thick near-black outer contour, intricate fine ink hatching, bold readable shadows and restrained textured color fills. Maintain the source's deep plum, burgundy, deep forest green, ochre-gold and brown palette where applicable. Do not switch to glossy digital painting, photorealism, anime or 3D rendering. Canvas: 1024x1536 portrait. Show exactly ONE complete figure, every foot and every piece of gear or flame/fume fully within the image, at least 3% safe white margin on EVERY side. Keep a compelling readable full-body silhouette. Background must be intentional PLAIN OPAQUE PURE WHITE (#FFFFFF), including every negative-space hole. No transparent checkerboard, no gradients, backdrop decoration, ground, floor or cast shadow, no text/UI/frame. Absolutely NO sunburst, radiating rays or halo baked into this portrait; the comparison backdrop is separate.
Subject: King, the imposing anthropomorphic brown BEAR WARRIOR. Preserve his broad bear muzzle, round ears, brown fur, powerful stocky bear proportions and broad fully visible clawed bear feet. Heavy angular dark-plum plate armor with aged ochre-gold raised edges and spikes, burgundy waistcloth, armored legs and forearm. His defining equipment is the massive jagged pointed dark-plum shield with gold edge and a large engraved GOLDEN SKULL. Show the entire shield. For this new take, refine the planted stance and weight distribution, turn the shield slightly into a clearer guard position, sharpen the proud wary face, and improve etched fur/plate detail while keeping the same character and recognisable equipment.
